hero.label: Codex Integration
hero.title: Bring RedNote & Douyin data into Codex: one MCP, one research skill
hero.description: MediaClaw gives Codex two things: a RedNote (Xiaohongshu) and Douyin MCP server whose 40+ tools collect posts, videos, comments and account data and dedupe them into structured results, and a content research skill whose 12 written methods handle teardowns, topic picks and drafting. Describe the goal in plain language; it follows the method, and it can read your local knowledge base at the same time. Before any new collection it states the source, volume and credit cost and waits for your go-ahead.
hero.tip: You need the MediaClaw browser extension installed and an active membership first. The agent can only use capabilities you approved in the extension, and every page visit still happens in your own browser.

tasks.title: What one sentence gets you once Codex is connected
tasks.description: All six are real MediaClaw Agent runs. The prompts are copy-ready — swap what's in angle brackets for your own. Every host runs the same MCP tools and the same methods, so the output is identical; the chat window in these screenshots may not match yours, but what comes back does.

items.title: Mine a comment section for topics you can write
items.description: “Pull at least 300 comments from this post, analyse what readers want, and tell me which topics I can take.” 322 comments deduped to 280, 35.4% of them explicit needs, delivered as a prioritized topic list and a multi-sheet workbook.

image.alt: Collecting RedNote comments and turning them into ranked topic ideas from Codex

items.title: Find low-follower, high-like accounts
items.description: “I just started an account and don't want to study 300k-follower creators. Find low-follower, high-like posts in this niche and tell me why they worked.” Four small accounts pulled from an 80-post sample, each with followers, top-post performance and what to learn.

image.alt: Codex surfacing low-follower high-like RedNote accounts with what to learn from each

items.title: See what a topic looks like across both platforms
items.description: “Check what new techniques people are posting about <keyword> on RedNote and Douyin lately.” It pins down which product the keyword means, reuses the existing RedNote sample, back-fills only Douyin, and groups recent patterns into 7 categories with examples.

image.alt: Codex running cross-platform topic research and grouping recent patterns into seven categories

items.title: Today's posts only — no last month's hits
items.description: “Show me RedNote posts about <keyword> published today.” 80 latest posts scanned as of 23:48, grouped by content direction with the current top performers listed. Put it on a daily schedule and it becomes lightweight monitoring.

image.alt: Codex pulling the day's newest RedNote posts and grouping them by direction

items.title: Tear down a video, then get a script you can shoot
items.description: “Why does this video keep people watching? How does the opening land and how does it build? Also turn it into a script I can shoot.” A precise teardown needs the transcript, so it quotes first (16 credits / 40 balance / an expiry), extracts only after you confirm, then returns the structure plus a 90-second script.

image.alt: Codex extracting a video's structure and handing back a shoot-ready 90-second script

items.title: Write the findings back into your own knowledge base
items.description: The one thing the extension cannot do alone. “File these comments into <knowledge base path> and put the conclusion at the top.” 1,000 comments land in the document, with core conclusions, theme signals, disagreements and unmet needs up front — and a reviewable diff before anything is written.

image.alt: Codex writing comment analysis into a local knowledge base document, conclusions first

setup.title: Getting connected: three steps, no terminal, no config file
setup.description: OS detection, chip detection, runtime download and checksum verification are all handled by Codex. You do two things: copy a prompt, and approve once.

items.title: Step 1: Copy the install prompt from the extension
items.description: Open System settings → Agent access in the extension, turn on “Allow local agents to call MediaClaw”, expand “Connect Agent”, and hit Copy on the Codex row. The prompt already carries the official source, the host's install commands and the repair steps — you do not need to read or edit it.

image.alt: MediaClaw's Agent access panel: enabling local agent calls and copying the Codex install prompt

items.title: Step 2: Send it to Codex and let it install itself
items.description: Paste it into a new conversation as-is. It registers the official marketplace, installs the package, detects Windows/macOS/Linux and x64/ARM64, then fetches and verifies the matching runtime. No Node install, no terminal, no picking a .exe — and it lists everything it did when it finishes.

image.alt: Codex installing and pairing on its own, listing every step it completed

items.title: Step 3: Approve the pairing back in the extension
items.description: A pending device appears in the Agent access tab. Check the device name and fingerprint, hit Approve, and Codex re-checks the connection by itself — no need to reply “approved”. Each agent is approved separately, and revoking one leaves the others alone.

image.alt: Verifying the device fingerprint and approving the Codex pairing in MediaClaw

items.question: Does driving it from Codex burn a lot of tokens?
items.answer: Less than you would expect. Collection, pagination and rate-limit cooldowns all run inside the extension and consume no host model quota — the extension hands back only structured results. Tokens go to three things: understanding the request, issuing calls and reading results, and the analysis and writing. It also reuses existing data before collecting anything new, and previews large payloads before paging into detail. A task that takes fifteen minutes is not fifteen minutes of token burn.

items.question: Is this an MCP? Do I have to write a config file?
items.answer: It is a standard MCP integration over STDIO, but on Codex you never write config. Send it the install prompt copied from the extension and it registers the official source, installs the package, detects your OS and chip, and verifies the runtime.

items.question: What is the difference between the skill and the MCP — do I install both?
items.answer: One install brings both. The MCP server exposes 40+ tools that fetch data from the platforms; the content research skill supplies 12 written methods that tell Codex how to analyse and write once the data is back. Tools without methods give you data with no conclusion.

items.question: Do I still need the browser extension after connecting Codex?
items.answer: Yes. The agent package cannot run on its own and does not replace the extension. Every page visit happens through the extension in your own browser, and the agent can only use capabilities you approved there.

items.question: Does my data pass through your servers?
items.answer: Collection runs in your own browser using the sessions you are already logged into; the session is never handed to the agent. Never paste cookies, tokens, activation codes or device keys into a conversation, issue or log — the agent will not ask for them.

items.question: Could it collect things or spend credits on its own?
items.answer: No. Before any new collection it states the source, time range, volume, what it will read and the cost boundary, and waits for your agreement. Billable capabilities such as transcripts show an estimated credit cost and balance for a second confirmation. Silence is never treated as consent, and anything beyond the approved scope is asked again.

items.question: How do upgrades work?
items.answer: In an existing MediaClaw conversation just say “upgrade MediaClaw Agent” — that sentence is the authorization. It refreshes the official source, installs, verifies the version and keeps your unfinished request. After install you must fully quit and reopen Codex: a running conversation cannot hot-load a new skill or MCP, and a new conversation in the same process does not count.

items.question: Will the skill collect data no matter what I ask?
items.answer: It reuses existing data first — analyses already in the extension, then the cloud workbench, then local collection records — and only considers new collection when none of those cover it. Say “don't use MediaClaw”, “don't call tools” or “only use the material I gave you” and it drops the tool chain. Requests unrelated to content research and creation never trigger it.

items.question: Is it free?
items.answer: The browser extension itself is free to use. Agent access requires an active membership, and billable capabilities such as video transcripts need credits plus a confirmation before they run. Analysis, generation and reporting on the agent side cost no MediaClaw credits.

items.question: How is this different from WorkBuddy or Doubao for Work?
items.answer: The capabilities are identical — same package, same MCP tools, same skill. Codex and WorkBuddy let the agent handle install and upgrades end to end. Doubao for Work has no automatic install entry yet, so you save a STDIO connector by hand under Skills · Connectors, and it does not auto-update.
